title: Do nearby targets imply nearby weights?
hook: Fit two almost coincident feature columns, then probe away from them.

doesNotKnow: Changing only the second target from 2 to 2.01 makes the coefficients…

claims.text: Do nearby targets imply nearby weights? Fit two almost coincident feature columns, then probe away from them. Changing only the second target from 2 to 2.01 makes the coefficients… Options: Stay at [2,0]; Move to [1,1]; Move to [0,2].

claims.text: A .01 target change moved the coefficients from [2,0] to [1,1]. The [2,2] probe stayed at 4; the [1,0] probe changed from 2 to 1. Identical columns admitted multiple coefficients. Stability along this observed relation did not ensure stability away from it.

claims.text: Why probe away from the relation between observed features? The two fitted coefficient pairs agree at [2,2] but disagree at [1,0]; on-support agreement alone conceals that difference.

claims.text:
Target / packet: `ai-correlated-coefficients` · `C2`. Prerequisites: `ai:linear-regression-fit`.

Nearest / distinct payoff: `linear-regression-fit` → `outlier-flattens-line` (existing registered artifact; evidence applicability pending). Unlike fitting one regression line, this isolates coefficient sensitivity while testing both in-support and off-support predictions.

Primary finite model: No-intercept X=[[1,1],[1,1.01]], y=[2,2]. Exact solution beta=[2,0]; change only second y to2.01 gives beta=[1,1]. Predictions on x=[1,1] remain2 and on[2,2] remain4.

Countercase and boundary: At x=[1,0], predictions2 versus1 diverge. Exactly identical columns make individual coefficients nonidentifiable; do not invert a singular matrix.

Predict and recall transfer: Predict coefficient stability under .01 perturbation; recall why predictions can remain stable along observed support but change off it.

Required evidence: Expose both fitted coefficients and on/off-support predictions; no claim of universally stable predictions under collinearity.
